name: Isoxsuprine

overview.mechanism: Has beta-adrenergic stimulant activity; vascular and obstetric effects should not be equated with established clinical benefit [[ISO-SPL]].
uses: Historically investigated for peripheral vascular symptoms. The cited US label lists historical “possibly effective” indications and explicitly is not FDA-approved labeling [[ISO-SPL]].

evidence.title: Clinical evidence and limitations
evidence.intro: Study regimens are descriptions of research, not prescribing recommendations.

rows.design: Double-blind crossover; 12 volunteers with and 12 without peripheral vascular disease.
rows.intervention: Single oral isoxsuprine administration versus placebo.
rows.findings: No significant increase in calf, foot or hand blood flow; claudication time was not prolonged.
rows.limitations: Small, older single-dose experiment; does not support a claim of demonstrated peripheral-vascular benefit or prevention of limb events.

sources.citation: Isoxsuprine Hydrochloride Tablets, USP; Vedco dba Valdar; DailyMed SPL revised January 2012. Label expressly states FDA has not found the drug safe and effective and has not approved this labeling.
Isoxsuprine as an oral vasodilator. PubMed PMID: 4599483.

draft_notes: Source-linked descriptive findings and safety information only. Current local product information, contraindications, formulation-specific dosing and renal schedules require verification.

revision_log.change: Added source-verified descriptive monograph, clinical evidence and safety limitations without unsupported dosing or inferred dialysis regimen.
revision_log.approved_by: W. G. M. Rivero, MD (delegated source-verification workflow; executed by Codex, 2026-11-25)

contraindications: The cited oral label states not to administer immediately postpartum or in the presence of arterial bleeding [[ISO-SPL]].

common: The label reports temporal associations with hypotension, tachycardia, chest pain, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, abdominal distress and severe rash; causality was not confirmed [[ISO-SPL]].
serious: Pulmonary edema has been reported in mothers treated with beta stimulants; maternal/fetal tachycardia and neonatal metabolic/hemodynamic complications are described with obstetric exposure [[ISO-SPL]].

monitoring: Discontinue if rash develops, as directed by the cited label [[ISO-SPL]].

pregnancy: The cited US label expressly states that isoxsuprine is neither approved nor recommended for premature labor [[ISO-SPL]].
renal: The vascular experiment did not establish renal dose adjustment, dialysis use or kidney benefit [[ISO-VASC]].
